reviews.title: Great value for the speed and capacity.
reviews.comment: -This 96GB 6400 kit has to be the current best value for size and speed. For ~$40 cheaper the "TEAMGROUP T-Force XTREEM DDR5 Ram 48GB" is a good kit with a faster 8000mhz rated speed, but at twice the capacity and with very little good alternatives at the 96GB+ size, this kit seems like a great value. -The first time I ordered this I had to return it due to my Gigabyte Aorus Ultra Z690 motherboard not wanting to boot with it. It was one of the very first z690 motherboards from when LGA1700 came out and seems to have a bad reputation with running RAM above ~5600. I got a replacement Asus z790 Gaming Wifi7 motherboard for $90 on ebay, and now I'm able to use this RAM kit in it with no issues at all; ran with its 6400 XMP on first boot and have seen 0 crashes or bluescreens after a few days. I may try overclocking it some more, but that seems pretty pointless with the great performance I'm already getting. -This is great RAM! Don't need all the flashy RGB and the smooth black color is fine with me!
reviews.author: J. Korbut

reviews.title: High Quality SK Hynix M die memory
reviews.comment: The RAM looks great, runs great, and runs cool.  I put it in my PC, enabled XMP, and it runs at the stock advertised speeds with no issues.  I was able to get it pretty easily to run at even better numbers without much of an issue, though I'm probably limited by my motherboard and CPU, all without needing to raise the voltage or do much beyond entering a few numbers in the bios. So to summarize- Looks sharp, has potential to run above spec, effective cooling, and in a nicely priced package.  Definitely recommend it to enthusiasts.
reviews.author: Bront

reviews.title: Garbage. Hot, hot garbage.
reviews.comment: 2x48gig, 6400@cl32 Only one of the modules would post. Tested numerous times in multiple slots. Module ending on 005 always gives a C5 error on my MSI tomahawk x870e, 006 always boots. Seems like they either fried the module when binning it and just didn't care if they sold it, or just binned just one module and called it good. Last team group product I am going to buy. It fails immediately, like nobody really binned this. EDIT: A few days later, the other module is starting to fail even at JEDEC speeds and below. I get random reboots, often leading to the fun C5 error. Running in Furmark (GPU) causes no issues, but Cyberpunk and Memtest86 will crash to C5. Cinebench made it to 9.5 minutes before a crash. Final update: bought comparative gskill ram (6000@30cl 2x48) $20 cheaper with a promo, they booted just fine and completed a pass of memtest86 with multicore. I rebooted multiple times while diagnosing an unrelated issue with igpu and Linux and there were no issues whatsoever with the new sticks. Seems that it definitely was two bad sticks of ram, seemingly both bad in different ways, and at $270 a kit you would think there would be more quality control. Tomorrow I go to the UPS store and send these back to the pit they came out of. Gskill please forgive me for betraying you.
